製.meaning: A clanking factory <part>system</part> of belts and blades swallows bolts of cloth at one end and spits out a finished <part>garment</part> every second. Each one gets the same little label sewn into the collar: <kanji>made in...</kanji> and the factory's name.
製.on: The finished shirts are locked in a huge steel <sound>sa</sound>fe until the trucks arrive.

花.meaning: A plain tuft of <part>grass</part> is tired of being stepped on, so one night it decides to <part>change</part>. It wriggles, stretches, and by morning a ring of bright yellow petals has burst out of its head. It's a <kanji>flower</kanji>.
花.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the pond next to it, just to get a sniff.
花.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs a passing bee, landing on it with a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an for a picnic.

増.meaning: The mole's hill was <part>formerly</part> one pinch of <part>soil</part>. Every night he adds another spadeful, and it grows to a hill, then a mountain, then a peak with snow on top. Every morning, watch it <kanji>increase</kanji>.
増.on: At the summit he paints a huge <sound>zo</sound>diac wheel round his telescope, sign after sign.
増.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, it's getting bigger!' he shouts down to his mother.

減.meaning: A <part>drill sergeant</part> orders his soldiers to drink up the <part>water drops</part> in the camp barrel. Gulp by gulp it empties, down to a puddle, then a drip, then a damp spot. The camp's supply starts to <kanji>dwindle</kanji>.
減.on: Then a bi<sound>g</sound> <sound>en</sound>gine pump gurgles up the very last drop.
減.kun: A thirsty <sound>he</sound>n pecks at the damp mud where the puddle used to be.

守.meaning: A grumpy grandma sits on the <part>roof</part> all night swinging a <part>golf club</part>, ready to bonk any burglar who climbs the drainpipe. Not one gets past her. She's the house's toughest <kanji>guard</kanji>.
守.on: She stays awake by crunching <sound>su</sound>gar cubes from her apron pocket.
守.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, we'll <sound>mo</sound>p the drainpipe with grease so nobody can climb it!' shout her grandkids.

確.meaning: Before you hang a <part>birdhouse</part>, you tie a heavy <part>stone</part> to it and let it swing all night in the storm. In the morning it's still there, not a nail loose. Now the birds can move in with total <kanji>assurance</kanji>.
確.on: Underneath it lies only a picked-clean fish <sound>carc</sound>ass that a crow dropped.
確.kun: To be extra sure, you throw a <sound>ta</sound>co at it, then duck behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld in case it bounces back.
